Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 1:

﴿Read﴾ (i.e., bring about the recitation), beginning ﴿in the name of your Lord who created﴾ the creatures.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 2:

﴿He created man﴾ the human species, ﴿from a clot﴾ plural of ʿalaqah (clot), which is a small piece of thick blood.

﴿Iqra'﴾ (Read) is an emphatic repetition of the first (imperative). ﴿Wa-rabbuka al-akram﴾ (And your Lord is the Most Generous), the One whom no generous one can equal. It is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring back to the pronoun in ﴿iqra'﴾.
﴿Who taught﴾ writing ﴿by the pen﴾. The first to write with it was Idris, peace be upon him.
﴿He taught man﴾ the human race ﴿what he did not know﴾ before being taught, of guidance, writing, crafts and other things.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 6:

﴿Indeed not!﴾ (truly) ﴿Indeed, man transgresses﴾

﴿That he saw himself﴾ means himself, ﴿self-sufficient﴾ through wealth. It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl. The verb *ra'a* (رَأى) is in the sense of knowing (*ʿilmiyya*), and *istaghna* (اسْتَغْنى) is its second object (*maf'ul thani*). The clause *an ra'ahu* (أنْ رَآهُ) is the object of cause or purpose (*maf'ul lahu*).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 8:

﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ O man, ﴿the return﴾, i.e., the returning (al-ruju') is a warning to him, so that He will recompense the tyrant (al-taghi) with what he deserves.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 9:

﴿Have you considered﴾ [the word ʾa-ra-ʾayta, "have you considered" or "have you seen"] is in three places for expressing amazement (taʿajjub), ﴿the one who forbids﴾ [i.e., the one who forbids] is Abu Jahl.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 10:

﴿a servant﴾ is the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿when he prays﴾
﴿Have you seen if he﴾ (was) the one forbidden ﴿upon guidance﴾
"Aw" is for division (the particle ﴿أوْ﴾ here is for distribution), ﴿commanded piety﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 13:

﴿Have you seen if he denies﴾ i.e., the one who forbids, the Prophet, ﴿and turns away﴾ from faith.

Qur'an 96:14: "Does he not know that Allah sees?" — what he has done. That is, He knows it and will repay him for it. That is, marvel at him, O listener, in respect of his forbidding the prayer, and in respect of the one forbidden being upon guidance and commanding piety, and in respect of the forbidder being one who denies and turns away from faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 15:

﴿Kallā﴾ a rebuke to him. ﴿La-in﴾ the lām is the lām of oath. ﴿Lam yantahi﴾ he does not desist from what he is upon of disbelief. ﴿La-nasfaʿan bi-l-nāṣiyah﴾ I will surely drag him by his forelock (nāṣiyah) into the Fire.

﴿Forelock﴾ is a *badal* (substitute, or apposition) of an indefinite noun (*nakira*) from a definite noun (*ma'rifa*). ﴿Lying, sinful﴾: describing it with this is a *majaz* (figurative usage), and what is meant is its owner.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 96, verse 17:

﴿So let him call upon his assembly.﴾ That is, the people of his assembly, and it is the nadi, the gathering place where the people converse and talk together. He had said to the Prophet (ﷺ), when the latter rebuked him for forbidding him to pray: "You know well that there is no man in this valley with more supporters than I. I will fill this valley against you with horses bare of hair and men without beards" (ʿalayka khayılan judan wa rijālan murdan, i.e., if you wish, horses and men).

﴿We shall call the guardians of hell﴾: the angels, harsh and severe, to destroy him, as in the hadith: "Had he called his assembly, the Zabaniyah (the angels of punishment) would have seized him openly."
﴿Nay﴾, a rebuke to him. ﴿Do not obey him﴾, O Muhammad, in abandoning the prayer. ﴿And prostrate﴾, that is, pray to God, ﴿and draw near﴾ to Him through obedience to Him.
